h1: The 5 Best 60V Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 genuine Greenworks 60V cordless leaf blowers scored on airflow, kit contents and turbo, from 450 CFM to 700 CFM brushless.
summary: The Greenworks 60V 700 CFM brushless is the strongest genuine 60V blower here and the one to buy for a big yard. The 610 CFM kit with a 2.5Ah battery is the better all-rounder if you do not own Greenworks batteries yet. Already have a 60V pack? Two bare-tool Greenworks Pro models save money, and the 450 CFM blower is the light-duty option.
intro: Greenworks sells its 60V outdoor line in two forms that look identical on a search page: complete kits with a battery and charger, and bare tools with nothing in the box. Choosing the wrong one is the most common mistake in this category. A bare blower is a good deal if you own 60V batteries, and a useless parcel if you do not.

This list keeps only genuine 60V blowers and ranks them on airflow, then on what comes in the box. We separated the kits from the bare tools clearly, since price comparisons between them mean nothing. Scores follow spec sheets and homeowner reports, nothing more.

products.name: Greenworks 60V 700 CFM Brushless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 700 CFM with a variable speed dial and turbo button. The strongest genuine 60V model here.
products.description:
This brushless blower reaches 700 CFM, the highest airflow among genuine 60V models in the group. A variable speed dial lets you tune power for patios or heavy leaves, and a turbo button adds a burst on demand.

It is the most expensive of the Greenworks blowers in the guide, and fewer buyers have used it than the older models. Against the 610 CFM kit, you gain about 90 CFM and a lighter, more comfortable grip, at a higher price.

Buy it if you have a large or tree-heavy yard and want maximum cordless push.
products.idealFor: Large yards with heavy leaf drop.
products.skipIf: You have a small yard or only light debris.

products.name: Greenworks 60V Electric Leaf Blower with 2.5Ah Battery
products.verdict: 610 CFM, 50 minutes on the included 2.5Ah battery, turbo up to 130 MPH.
products.description:
Where most of the Greenworks 60V listings here are bare tools, this one arrives with a 2.5Ah battery, which the listing says gives about 50 minutes of runtime. Airflow is 610 CFM, with a turbo mode that raises air speed to 130 MPH for stubborn debris.

It ranks second because it asks more in price than the bare tools, but you get a working blower in one box. Against the 700 CFM, it is less powerful and has the same kit advantage. The listing also claims quieter operation than gas.

The pick for anyone starting a Greenworks 60V collection from scratch.

products.name: Greenworks Pro Bare Tool 60V 610 CFM GEN2 Blower
products.verdict: 610 CFM with turbo and a concentrator nozzle, sold without battery or charger.
products.description:
This GEN2 Greenworks Pro delivers 610 CFM and includes a turbo mode that loosens wet leaves, plus a concentrator nozzle that speeds up the airstream on stubborn debris.

It is sold bare, so you must already own a 60V battery and charger. That makes it good value for existing owners and a bad buy for newcomers. Against the kit above, it saves money if you already have the pack.

Best for existing Greenworks owners who want a stronger blower without buying another battery.
pros: Saves money with your own pack
products.idealFor: Greenworks owners who already have 60V batteries.

products.name: Greenworks Pro Bare Tool 60V 540 CFM Blower
products.verdict: The lowest price here, with a brushless motor and cruise control, as a bare tool.
products.description:
The older Greenworks Pro offers 540 CFM, a brushless motor and a variable speed trigger with cruise control. The motor is built for power and quieter running.

It costs the least in the group, but battery and charger are not included. The 610 CFM bare tool beats it on airflow for a small step up, so this one ranks lower unless price is the main limit.

A cost-saving option for owners with 60V batteries and a modest yard.
products.idealFor: 60V owners on a tight budget with a smaller yard.
products.skipIf: You need a battery in the box.

products.name: Greenworks 60V Electric Leaf Blower (450 CFM)
products.verdict: The lowest airflow here at 450 CFM, with adjustable wind power for varied tasks.
products.description:
This blower provides 450 CFM, the lowest in the group, with adjustable wind power to match the job. It is rated for multi-scene use beyond just leaves, such as patios and driveways.

It ranks last because airflow is what a leaf blower is for, and the 540 and 610 models offer more. Wet or packed leaves will test it.

A light-duty choice for small yards and hard surfaces.

whatMatters.detail: A bare tool has no battery or charger, so it only works if you already own a compatible Greenworks 60V pack. A kit includes both. Read the title for the words 'bare tool' or 'with battery' before ordering, because this decides whether the box contains a working blower.
CFM tells you how much air moves, which clears piles. MPH tells you how hard it hits, which loosens stuck debris. Between 540 and 700 CFM suits most yards, and below 500 is for light work.
A 2.5Ah pack gives a listed runtime of around 50 minutes at normal speed, and turbo drains it faster. For a big yard consider a larger pack or a second battery.
Brushless motors run quieter and tend to last longer than brushed ones. They are listed on the 540 and 700 CFM models. Check the specs for the word brushless rather than assuming.
You hold a blower at arm's length for long periods, so balance matters. A lightweight design with a comfortable grip reduces fatigue. Compare listed weights, and remember the battery adds to it.

faq.q: Do I need to buy a battery separately?
faq.a: For the two Greenworks Pro bare tools, yes. The 2.5Ah kit includes one. Always read the listing title.
They are different platforms, not better or worse on voltage alone. Pick the one that matches batteries you own or the tool range you want.
540 to 700 CFM suits most yards. The 450 CFM model is for light work.
A brushless motor runs quieter and tends to last longer. The 700 CFM and 540 CFM Greenworks models list it.

faq.q: How long will the 2.5Ah battery last?
faq.a: The listing says about 50 minutes, but turbo mode runs it down faster.

faq.q: Can I use an EGO battery on a Greenworks blower?
faq.a: No. Batteries are specific to each brand and platform.

finalTake: The Greenworks 60V 700 CFM Brushless is the best 60V leaf blower for large yards. If you are starting from nothing, the 2.5Ah kit is the safer buy because the battery is in the box. Owners with 60V packs can save with the Greenworks Pro 610 CFM GEN2 bare tool.
